evidence.claim: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.title: Anayasa | Anayasa Mahkemesi
evidence.excerpt: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text governing the 2022 presidency; direct and stable legal authority/constraint source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Erdoğan's office-level authority and checks in 2022; not a claim about personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same articles constrain decree power and preserve parliamentary/judicial checks.
Formal authority does not prove how he used it in practice.

evidence.claim: Parliament passed a law sought by President Erdoğan's ruling party that allows jail sentences for false or misleading information, and the main opposition said its leader became the first target after criticizing authorities over a drug 'epidemic'.
evidence.title: Erdogan rival is first target of Turkish media law, opposition party says
evidence.excerpt: Parliament passed a law sought by President Erdoğan's ruling party that allows jail sentences for false or misleading information, and the main opposition said its leader became the first target after criticizing authorities over a drug 'epidemic'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with explicit attribution to the ruling party and the first enforcement target.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, shortly before the next election cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the law was sought by Erdoğan's party and was used against criticism of state conduct.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the law as a response to false information.
A legal challenge or prosecution is not itself proof that Erdoğan personally authored the complaint.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan appointed Nureddin Nebati, a strong supporter of the low-interest-rate line, as treasury and finance minister, replacing the last top official seen to favor orthodox policy, and Reuters noted he had already fired three central bank governors since mid-2019.
evidence.title: Erdogan picks low-rates champion as finance minister as Turkish lira skids
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan appointed Nureddin Nebati, a strong supporter of the low-interest-rate line, as treasury and finance minister, replacing the last top official seen to favor orthodox policy, and Reuters noted he had already fired three central bank governors since mid-2019.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters directly ties the appointment to Erdoğan's control over the economic team and describes the loyalty/orthodoxy pattern.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited into 2022 and still governing in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is Erdoğan's appointment decision and part of his broader personnel control over economic policy.
contrary_evidence: Nebati had prior government experience as a deputy finance minister.
Appointment alone does not prove personal enrichment, only loyalty and policy alignment.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan proposed putting a headscarf constitutional amendment to referendum, and Reuters reported that critics saw the move as an attempt to outflank the opposition, with the real target being the LGBT+ community rather than the stated women's-rights framing.
evidence.title: Erdogan moots putting Turkey headscarf reform to referendum
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan proposed putting a headscarf constitutional amendment to referendum, and Reuters reported that critics saw the move as an attempt to outflank the opposition, with the real target being the LGBT+ community rather than the stated women's-rights framing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is solid on the statement and the political reading, though the opportunism inference is interpretive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to high: the proposal was Erdoğan's own public move, but the opportunism reading is partly interpretive.
contrary_evidence: The proposal was formally framed as protecting women's right to wear a headscarf.
The issue had genuine rights-history context in Turkey, so the move was not purely fabricated.

evidence.claim: After Berat Albayrak resigned, newsroom managers told staff not to report it until the government said so, and pro-government outlets stayed silent for more than 24 hours, illustrating Erdoğan-era media control and self-censorship.
evidence.title: Special Report-Insiders reveal how Erdogan tamed Turkey's newsrooms
evidence.excerpt: After Berat Albayrak resigned, newsroom managers told staff not to report it until the government said so, and pro-government outlets stayed silent for more than 24 hours, illustrating Erdoğan-era media control and self-censorship.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reported directly from newsroom insiders and media sources; the episode is older than 2022 but the report documents a continuing control mechanism relevant to 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022; underlying incident is 2020, but the mechanism is relevant to 2022 conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the conduct concerns a family-linked resignation and a media environment shaped by Erdoğan; it does not prove a specific falsehood by Erdoğan himself.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show Erdoğan personally ordered the silence.
It is media-control evidence, not a direct asset or gift record.

evidence.claim: Lawmakers debated a media bill proposed by Erdoğan's AK Party that critics said would intensify the crackdown on critical reporting and allow prison sentences for spreading false information about Turkey's security.
evidence.title: Turkey's parliament debates Erdogan's media 'disinformation' bill
evidence.excerpt: Lawmakers debated a media bill proposed by Erdoğan's AK Party that critics said would intensify the crackdown on critical reporting and allow prison sentences for spreading false information about Turkey's security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting quoted the bill and its legislative context directly; this is a contemporaneous 2022 policy action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for agenda-setting and sponsorship of the bill; the article attributes the proposal to his party and majority, not to a personal draft by Erdoğan.
contrary_evidence: Government defenders said the law was meant to protect people from false accusations and disinformation.
The article does not prove the law was used against a specific truth-teller in this case.

evidence.claim: After allegations about some questions in the 2022 KPSS exam, Erdoğan ordered the State Supervisory Board to investigate and said the findings would be assessed and necessary steps taken.
evidence.title: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, 2022 KPSS Lisans oturumuna ilişkin DDK’ye inceleme talimatı verdi
evidence.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications
evidence.excerpt: After allegations about some questions in the 2022 KPSS exam, Erdoğan ordered the State Supervisory Board to investigate and said the findings would be assessed and necessary steps taken.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The official presidency communications page records the directive and the quotation; it proves the response, not the underlying allegations.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 response to a domestic integrity allegation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the directive is attributed to Erdoğan personally, but it is a procedural response rather than an admission of his own false statement or corruption.
contrary_evidence: The page does not say Erdoğan admitted wrongdoing or corrected a prior false claim.
It concerns an exam-integrity allegation, not assets or gifts.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
